task_contract.anchor_definition: The anchor is the first target-specific byte-array value-construction function on the dynamic behavior chain: the earliest function, after routing, batch configuration collection, runtime state collection and input preparation, whose own body constructs the target observable batch_payload value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, packaging the result, or emitting it to the sink.

candidate_scope.included_note: Paths are relative to agent_visible/, matching task.json visible_corpus.

runtime_boundary.event_plane: DOM CustomEvent on the main document

evidence: The DevTools-visible JavaScript corpus is a single obfuscated bundle and no source map is exposed to the agent.
The target field name is assembled from character-code arrays at the sink, so direct literal search is insufficient.
The target byte payload is carried through runtime-derived transport keys and recovered shortly before console output.
The live byte-conversion configuration is selected only after the prescribed #encodeButton click, once click-time DOM, form-order, style and dataset state are captured.

Function names related to byte-array construction remain intentionally visible for answerability; the intended difficulty is semantic disambiguation among the byte candidates, not hiding every relevant identifier.

The target path crosses delegated event handling, two-stage action routing, staged-state gate checks, tuple construction, asynchronous scheduling, local event dispatch, runtime slot materialization, byte-array conversion, dynamic transport and sink wrapping.
The same batch.encode interaction produces non-target preview/audit objects carrying batch_payload-like values before the target batch.encode object.
The deployed bundle also contains proof-like, state-like and vendor-like decoys that execute or remain reachable-looking without feeding the target batch_payload field.
The target value is separated from the #encodeButton click by Promise, microtask, timer, animation-frame, MutationObserver and DOM CustomEvent boundaries.
The selected runtime configuration is cloned and mutated in a WeakMap-backed materialization step before the byte converter receives it.
The final sink receives an already encoded byte payload after dynamic cell and lane recovery, so sink inspection alone does not identify the construction site.

behavior_category.reason: The observable value is produced by materializing a runtime-dependent byte array and encoding it as a stable byte payload string. It is not a request signature, browser fingerprint, plain state encoding or request-body rewrite.

near_categories.why_not: The output has no proof/token/seal semantics; proof-like code in the bundle is decoy material and does not feed the target field.
The target specifically constructs a byte array and serializes it as a byte payload rather than only formatting UI state.
No network request body is emitted or rewritten; the target is a console-observable byte payload.
The chain uses local DOM and form state, not browser/device capability collection as the target behavior.
